bull.b: The Anthropic agreement materially improves revenue visibility and shifts the business toward contracted AI infrastructure. Its long duration and scale can support financing, capacity expansion and more predictable cash generation as deployment progresses.

Rapid HPC leasing growth demonstrates a durable transition beyond Bitcoin mining toward higher-value computing infrastructure. Additional Lake Mariner capacity and contracted projects provide a pipeline for continued revenue expansion if commissioning schedules are met.

Substantial liquidity and proceeds from monetizing Abernathy give TeraWulf funding flexibility for committed construction and strategic expansion. Capital recycling toward wholly owned campuses may improve control and long-term economics while reducing reliance on new equity.

bear.b: Deep losses and persistently negative cash generation show that the current business is not self-funding. Until new HPC capacity reaches scale and costs normalize, continued investment and operating deficits could require substantial external financing.

Very high leverage and an extremely thin reported equity base reduce financial flexibility and increase sensitivity to execution setbacks. Debt obligations may constrain future investment, while additional funding could create dilution or refinancing risk.

The growth plan depends on delivering large, technically complex data-center projects on schedule. Skilled-labor shortages and evolving tenant requirements can delay revenue activation, raise construction costs and weaken returns on committed capital.
